_comments: Sample configuration for Databricks (EXPERIMENTAL — not yet verified end-to-end).
Replace <host>, <http_path>, and <token> with your Databricks workspace values.
db_schema: set to the target schema/database in your Databricks workspace.
DRIVER VERSION (updated 2026-08-31, confirmed via a live measurement in this project):
Use the databricks-jdbc 2.6.x line (2.6.40 confirmed loadable and working) -- NOT 3.x.
Both orm_skyway's and Gilhari's Docker images run JDK 8. databricks-jdbc 3.x's driver
class is compiled for Java 11 (class-file major version 55, over JDK 8's limit of 52)
and fails to load at all -- a hard class-load failure, not a degraded connection.
Both driver generations register the IDENTICAL class name
(com.databricks.client.jdbc.Driver), so nothing in this config will reveal which one
is actually installed if you download the wrong one -- check the jar itself.
Download from https://www.databricks.com/spark/jdbc-drivers-download or
com.databricks:databricks-jdbc on Maven Central; pin to a 2.6.x release explicitly.
URL QUOTING: a Databricks JDBC URL is semicolon-separated by construction
(transportMode=http;ssl=1;httpPath=...;AuthMech=3). Wrapping the URL portion in ASCII
single quotes, as below, stops JDX's own JDX_DATABASE line parser from misreading those
semicolons as its own field separators -- the same mechanism already documented for Db2
in configuration.md's 'Advanced: driver connection properties in the URL' section.
orm_skyway >=1.0.34 strips the quotes automatically for its own direct JDBC calls while
preserving them in the generated line, so this is safe to leave in place unconditionally.
Copy to your project root, rename to orm_skyway_config.json, and edit for your database.
Run: python orm_skyway.py -f orm_skyway_config.json --phase 1+3
